response:
feat(CC-0116): scope service DB credentials per ControlPlane

- Add reconcileDBCredentials sub-reconciler that, in managed mode,
  projects a per-ControlPlane OpenBao-backed ExternalSecret named
  {name}-keystone-db-credentials reading the namespace+name-scoped path
  openstack/keystone/{namespace}/{name}/db, so two ControlPlanes never
  collide on the cluster-global OpenBao backend
- Drive DBCredentialsReady on the ControlPlane: True once the
  ExternalSecret syncs, False with WaitingForDBCredentialSecret while it
  requeues, and True immediately in brownfield mode (reason
  BrownfieldUserSuppliedCredential) where the operator projects nothing
- Owner-reference the projected ExternalSecret to the ControlPlane so it
  is garbage-collected with the CR while ESO owns the materialised Secret
- Insert DBCredentials into the sub-reconciler chain after Infrastructure
  and before Keystone, register it in subConditionTypes and the metrics
  instrumentation map, and give it a dedicated 10s requeue interval, so
  Keystone is never projected before its DB credential Secret exists
- Override the projected Keystone CR's database.secretRef in managed mode
  to the operator-owned per-ControlPlane Secret (key "password") while
  leaving cp.Spec untouched; brownfield keeps the user-supplied secretRef
- Seed per-ControlPlane DB credentials in write-bootstrap-secrets.sh at
  openstack/keystone/{namespace}/{name}/db for each KORC_CONTROLPLANES
  identity and drop the flat openstack/keystone/db seed
- Remove the static keystone-db ExternalSecret from the production deploy
  stack and add a kind-only keystone-db ExternalSecret pinned to the
  default identity's per-CP path to keep standalone Keystone flows working
- Grant the c5c3-operator create/update on externalsecrets (asserted by
  Helm clusterrole/role unit tests) so it can CreateOrUpdate the
  per-ControlPlane ExternalSecret
- Cover the reconciler with unit tests for managed projection shape,
  brownfield no-op, requeue/ready conditions, and distinct per-CP remote
  key and Secret name, plus Keystone secretRef-override tests for both modes
- Add integration tests proving the DB-credential gate blocks Keystone
  until the ExternalSecret is Ready and that two ControlPlanes resolve to
  distinct DB-credential paths and Secret names
- Add the presence-guarded db-credential-scoping chainsaw E2E test and
  repoint the existing keystone E2E fixtures off the removed flat path to
  openstack/keystone/openstack/controlplane/db
- Document the operator-owned database.secretRef contract and per-CP
  OpenBao path across the ControlPlane CRD, reconciler, OpenBao bootstrap,
  Quick Start, and Keystone E2E references; note that existing eso-management
  and eso-control-plane policy wildcards already cover the per-CP path
